claims.text: The unified stress–strain and thermoelastic behavior of HfNbTaTiZr is governed by processing-induced residual stresses arising from thermal-expansion mismatch between microstructurally distinct regions.
Undistorted, cold-worked, and aged regions in HfNbTaTiZr have sufficiently different effective thermal-expansion coefficients to create internal mismatch.
Differential thermal expansion between microstructural regions generates internal residual-stress fields during processing and heat treatment.
The internal residual stresses alter energy barriers for dislocation motion.
The internal residual stresses alter phase evolution, including localized transformation or precipitation.
Residual-stress-mediated dislocation and phase evolution governs the alloy's tensile-creep behavior.
Residual-stress-mediated dislocation and phase evolution governs the alloy's temperature-dependent elastic moduli.
Residual-stress-mediated dislocation and phase evolution governs the alloy's hardening behavior.
The as-cast HfNbTaTiZr initial state is a single BCC phase.
As-cast HfNbTaTiZr has an inherent dendritic structure.
The as-cast initial state has minimal thermal residual stress.
Cold-worked regions have higher dislocation densities than less-distorted regions.
Cold-worked or aged regions may contain strain-induced transformed material or precipitates.
Increasing thermal-expansion mismatch will increase yield strength relative to the baseline.
Increasing thermal-expansion mismatch will enhance work hardening relative to the baseline.
Increasing thermal-expansion mismatch will improve creep resistance near 1250 °C.
Increasing thermal-expansion mismatch will systematically shift elastic moduli measured from 293 to 1100 K.
Specimens with minimized thermal-expansion mismatch will approach the base-state mechanical and thermoelastic behavior.
Thermal-expansion mismatch during composite solidification induces thermal stresses that affect strength.
Hardening and microstructural evolution occur during aging in the 600–800 °C range.
